A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Synthetic-Domain Alignment (SDA) work and retain matching ImageNet experiments. Their main texts, equations, figures, tables and appendices are readable and support comparison despite substantial restructuring.

before.justification: v1 reports original SDA results on ImageNet-C and ImageNet-W, component and hyperparameter ablations, timing measurements, and appendix data-sensitivity experiments.

after.justification: v2 retains original SDA experiments and adds source-image alignment tests, CIFAR-10-C, segmentation, LLaVA and expanded data-stream evaluations.

M1.justification: The SDA procedure remains conditional generation, unconditional diffusion alignment, synthetic-data fine-tuning, target-data adaptation and prediction ensembling. v2 names the existing generation/alignment process Mix of Diffusion and explicitly includes source pretraining in its diagram. These changes and the additional experimental instantiations do not establish a revised SDA algorithm.

E1.justification: Beyond the retained ImageNet-C/W classification coverage, v2 adds CIFAR-10-C, PASCAL VOC-C semantic segmentation and four-option language-based classification with LLaVA on ImageNet-C. Its UniTTA evaluation also extends the earlier stream tests to broader class/domain correlation and imbalance scenarios.

E2.justification: The stream comparison adds ROID, NOTE, CoTTA, TRIBE, BN, UnMIX, RoTTA, LAME and UniTTA alongside retained TENT and DDA, while dropping MEMO, DiffPure and GDA from that comparison. DiffPure also disappears from the four detailed classifier comparisons in v1 Figure 5 versus v2 Tables 13–16. The headline ImageNet comparator sets remain unchanged.

E3.justification: The earlier batch-size 1/64 stream tests on three classifiers are replaced by averages over 12 UniTTA settings using ResNet-50. New protocols include source-image accuracy across diffusion timesteps, FID measurements, segmentation evaluated with mIoU, and four-option LLaVA evaluation with zero-shot and fine-tuned controls. The original ImageNet 50K-image, 15-epoch adaptation settings are retained.

E4.justification: v2 adds a source-image control examining diffusion-induced misalignment, timestep/FID analyses and substantially expanded stream robustness tests. It removes the timing comparison, classifier-free-guidance ablation, ImageNet-W portions of the component and data-volume ablations, and four supplementary Grad-CAM cases. The two main Grad-CAM examples are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental seed counts, repeated-run uncertainty, confidence intervals or significance tests. The prediction confidence scores removed from the Grad-CAM displays are not estimates of experimental uncertainty.

E6.justification: New experiments report SDA/DDA results of 72.4/65.3 accuracy on CIFAR-10-C, 39.8/38.6 mIoU on VOC-C and 93.6/91.2 accuracy for LLaVA. Original SDA ImageNet scores persist, but Swin-T Source changes from 33.1 to 33.5, and conditional-only Swin-T/ConvNeXt-T scores change from 39.2/44.2 to 40.1/44.6 without an explanation of reruns. The detailed ConvNeXt-B Source average changes from 45.6 to 46.1, although v2 Table 3 still reports 45.6. Stream results are replaced under different settings, and several ablation, timing and qualitative results disappear.

T1.justification: v2 adds a KL-divergence contraction relation attributed to prior work, formal minimum-timestep reasoning and a noisy-distribution approximation for conditional-to-unconditional alignment. v1 provides mainly qualitative convergence motivation and includes a generic diffusion-training loss that v2 omits. No new theorem or proof is introduced.

C1.justification: The central contribution and claim that synthetic-domain alignment improves diffusion-driven TTA remain intact. The abstract and conclusion now explicitly extend the demonstrated performance claim to segmenters and MLLMs, broadening the earlier classifier-centered evidence without redefining the central contribution.

C2.justification: v2 develops the interpretation that visually faithful diffusion reconstructions can still be strongly misaligned with source models, separating this issue from target corruption in Section 3.2. Conversely, it removes v1's explicit discussion of slow inference, adaptation overhead and potentially missing task-relevant synthetic attributes, along with the specific contrast-corruption failure explanation. The general caveat that adapted images can be less recognizable remains.

D1.justification: v2 Table 12 adds CIFAR/VOC optimizers, learning rates, batch sizes, training budgets and diffusion settings; the supplement also documents the LLaVA task format and references its fine-tuning defaults. Some ImageNet details are relocated, but measured generation/alignment/fine-tuning times, the 80GB GPU specification and the ResNet decay factor are removed. The code-access link is unchanged.

R1.justification: The cited research context expands substantially around realistic continual TTA and the new task/model experiments, including UniTTA, additional traditional TTA methods, LLaVA, Dataset Diffusion, FLUX and EDM. Several earlier synthetic-data examples and generated-image-detection references are removed. The central positioning as complementary to DDA/GDA is retained.

P1.justification: The introduction, related work and method exposition are extensively rewritten. Separate preliminaries and framework sections become an integrated Methodology section; experiments gain a scalability subsection, the Discussion section disappears, and the appendices are reorganized. Mix of Diffusion terminology is introduced, and the author list changes.

P2.justification: v2 adopts a two-column layout and substantially redraws the framework diagrams. The corruption bar charts become numerical tables, existing ablation tables lose their ImageNet-W columns, and the retained Grad-CAM display is reformatted without confidence scores. New control, scalability, stream and timestep displays appear, while timing, guidance-scale and supplementary visualization displays are removed.

improvement.justification: v2 gives the central alignment argument a more direct source-image control in Section 3.2/Table 2 and tests applicability beyond ImageNet classifiers through segmentation, LLaVA and broader stream comparisons. These address important limitations of v1's largely classification-based and indirect mechanistic evidence. Removed runtime/limitations disclosure, reduced ablation coverage and some numerical inconsistencies weaken transparency, but the stronger tests of the central explanation and applicability provide a substantial net improvement.
